title: Philidor Defense: the ideas
line: A pawn guards the center pawn: solid, with less room for the pieces.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its king two squares, into the center.
Push your king pawn two squares too. It takes your share of the center.

also.c7c5: That is the Sicilian Defense, also sound. This lesson pushes the king pawn.
also.e7e6: That is the French Defense, also sound. This lesson pushes the king pawn.
also.c7c6: That is the Caro-Kann Defense, also sound. This lesson pushes the king pawn.

steps.text: Guard the pawn with a pawn: move the pawn in front of your queen one square.

also.b8c6: Guarding with the knight is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson guards with the pawn.
also.g8f6: That is Petrov's Defense, also sound. This lesson guards the pawn.

steps.after: This is the Philidor Defense: solid, but it shuts in your bishop on f8, and masters seldom choose it. White attacks the pawn again.

steps.text: Take the pawn on d4. You give up the center, but your pieces get free squares.

also.g8f6: That is also played. This lesson takes the pawn.
also.b8d7: Keeping the pawn on e5 is the Hanham Variation, a lesson of its own. This lesson takes.

steps.text: Bring the knight out to attack White's pawn on e4.
Bring the bishop out to e7, the square the pawn left free. It clears the way to castle.
Castle. Your king leaves the center, where White has more room.

also.b8c6: That is also played. This lesson castles first.

steps.text: Move the pawn on c7 one square. Next your queen pawn can go to d5 and strike at the center.

also.a7a6: That is also played. This lesson gets the push in the center ready.
also.f8e8: That is also played. This lesson gets the push in the center ready.

steps.after: White has more room. Black stays solid, and the pawn push to d5 is its way to fight back.

summary: A pawn guards the center pawn. Black gives up the center, brings its pieces out, and waits for its pawn break.
